children: , formerly FleetCor, and its CEO Ronald Clarke have agreed to pay $100M to settle a Federal Trade Commission administrative action for allegedly charging unauthorized fees.

According to a complaint filed by the FTC in 2019, Corpay charged its customers unauthorized fees, which they never knew about and did not agree to pay, and late fees in instances when customers had either paid on time or were prevented by the company from paying on time.
Furthermore, the company that sold fuel card services is said to have misrepresented the gas savings, fraud-control features, and fees associated with its fuel cards.

"FleetCor deceived its small business customers by promising fuel savings that never materialized, while unfairly charging them hidden and unauthorized fees," said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection.
The $100M settlement will be used to provide redress to the company's business customers harmed by its practices, the regulator said, noting reimposition of a federal court injunction against Clarke.

title: Corpay, CEO to pay $100M to settle FTC action over unauthorized fees
